title: Merge or rebase the same two branches
objective: Predict where each branch and HEAD point after merge or rebase, and say which command rewrites commits.
summary: A walkthrough and a stepper start from the same fork: C3 on feature and C4 on main, both children of C2. Merge records commit C5 with two parents and rewrites nothing. Rebase replays C3 as a new commit C3' on top of C4, so history is a straight line. A third start shows a merge that stops on a conflict until you edit, add and commit.

watch.transcript:
# Merge and rebase on the same fork

Commits C1 and C2 sit on main. The branch feature adds C3 and main adds C4, both with the parent C2. On main, git merge feature records a merge commit C5 with the two parents C4 and C3. On feature, git rebase main replays C3 on top of C4 as a new commit C3', so history is a straight line. Both give the same final files, so rebase only commits that exist only in your repository.

**00:00 Commits, branches and HEAD.** Each commit stores a snapshot and a link to its parent. A branch is a movable pointer, and HEAD names your current branch.

**00:10 One history forks into two.** Now the history forks into two lines. Feature adds C3, main adds C4, and both commits have the parent C2.

**00:19 git merge feature, on main.** On main, git merge feature combines C4, C3 and their common ancestor C2. Git records C5, a merge commit with two parents.

**00:29 git rebase main, on feature.** On feature, git rebase main replays the change of C3 on top of C4 as a new commit, C3'. History becomes a straight line.

**00:39 Same files, different history.** Both commands give the same final files, but rebase rewrites commits. Never rebase commits that exist outside your repository.

Sources:

- Pro Git — https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2

props.title: git merge feature, on main

frames.caption: Start: main and feature both grow from C2. HEAD is on main, and main points to C4.
git merge feature finds C2, the common ancestor of the two tips C4 and C3.
Git records merge commit C5 with two parents, C4 and C3, and moves main to C5.
feature still points to C3. Both lines of work stay in the history, joined by C5.

props.code:
git checkout main
git merge feature

merge.title: git merge feature, on main

frames.caption: Start: main and feature both grow from C2. HEAD is on main, and main points to C4.
git merge feature finds C2, the common ancestor of the two tips C4 and C3.
Git records merge commit C5 with two parents, C4 and C3, and moves main to C5.
feature still points to C3. Both lines of work stay in the history, joined by C5.

merge.code:
git checkout main
git merge feature

rebase.title: git rebase main, on feature

frames.caption: Start on feature: HEAD is on feature at C3, and main has moved on to C4.
git rebase main finds the common ancestor C2 and saves the change that C3 made.
Git resets feature to C4 and applies the saved change as a new commit C3' with the parent C4.
On main, git merge feature is a fast-forward: main moves to C3'. History is one straight line.

rebase.code:
git checkout feature
git rebase main
git checkout main
git merge feature

conflict.title: A merge that stops on a conflict

frames.caption: C3 and C4 both changed the same line of one file. HEAD is on main at C4.
git merge feature stops: Git cannot choose between the two versions, so it records no commit yet.
You edit the file: keep the correct line and delete the conflict markers.
git add marks the conflict in that file as resolved.
git commit records merge commit C5 with parents C4 and C3, and main moves to C5.

conflict.code:
git checkout main
git merge feature
# edit the file: keep one version, delete the markers
git add <file>
git commit

checkpoints.prompt: HEAD is on feature and you run git commit. What moves?

choices.text: feature moves to the new commit; HEAD still names feature
HEAD moves to the new commit; feature stays where it was
choices.misconception: Thinks HEAD points at a commit instead of at the current branch

choices.text: Every branch moves to the new commit
choices.misconception: Thinks all branches share one pointer instead of each being its own pointer

checkpoints.explanation: HEAD points to the branch you are on, and a new commit moves only that branch pointer forward. Other branches keep pointing at their own commits.

checkpoints.prompt: HEAD is on main at C4. You run git merge feature, and feature points to C3. Where does main point afterwards?

choices.text: To a new merge commit C5 with parents C4 and C3
To C3, the tip of feature
choices.misconception: Expects a fast-forward, which happens only when the other branch is directly ahead
Thinks merge changes files but never moves the branch pointer

checkpoints.explanation: The histories diverged at C2, so Git does a three-way merge of C4, C3 and C2 and records merge commit C5 with two parents. The current branch, main, moves to C5.

checkpoints.prompt: HEAD is on feature at C3. You run git rebase main. What does feature point to afterwards?

choices.text: A new commit C3' whose parent is C4
The same commit C3, now with the parent C4
choices.misconception: Thinks rebase edits an existing commit in place instead of creating a new one

choices.text: A merge commit with parents C3 and C4
choices.misconception: Confuses rebase with merge, which records a commit with two parents

checkpoints.explanation: Rebase saves the change C3 made, resets feature to C4 and applies the change as a new commit C3'. A commit's parent is part of the commit, so a new parent means a new commit.

checkpoints.prompt: Load the conflict start, where C3 and C4 changed the same line. Step until Git records the merge commit.

goal.hint: Press Forward until the status reads merge done.

checkpoints.explanation: When both sides edit the same part of a file, Git pauses the merge and writes conflict markers. The merge ends only after you edit the file, run git add, then git commit.

checkpoints.prompt: You pushed feature, and a teammate built work on it. Which history change is safe now?

choices.text: Merge main into it, because merge rewrites no commits
Rebase it onto main and push again
choices.misconception: Thinks rebase keeps the same commits, but it creates new ones that duplicate the teammate copies

choices.text: Either one, because the final files are the same
choices.misconception: Thinks the same final snapshot means the same history

checkpoints.explanation: Rebase replaces commits with new ones. Teammates who hold the old commits get duplicates at their next pull. Pro Git: do not rebase commits that exist outside your repository.
